reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
name: Pfirrmann Grading of Disc Degeneration

version.label: Pfirrmann et al. (2001), grades I–V
version.detail: Lumbar discs on T2-weighted MRI. The 8-level modified grading (Griffith et al. 2007) is a different system.

purpose: Grades lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration on T2-weighted MRI.

options.label: Grade I
options.detail: Homogeneous, bright white; clear nucleus–annulus distinction; normal height.

options.label: Grade II
options.detail: Inhomogeneous, with or without horizontal bands; clear distinction; normal height.

options.label: Grade III
options.detail: Inhomogeneous, grey; distinction unclear; height normal or slightly decreased.

options.label: Grade IV
options.detail: Inhomogeneous, grey to black; distinction lost; height normal to moderately decreased.

options.label: Grade V
options.detail: Inhomogeneous, black; distinction lost; disc space collapsed.

resultStates.label: Grade I
resultStates.summary: Homogeneous, bright white; clear nucleus–annulus distinction; normal height.

resultStates.label: Grade II

resultStates.label: Grade III

resultStates.label: Grade IV

resultStates.label: Grade V
resultStates.summary: Inhomogeneous, black; distinction lost; disc space collapsed.

clinicalContext.text: Describes disc degeneration; degeneration is common without symptoms.

limitations.text: Imaging findings correlate poorly with pain.

limitations: Reliability lower between grades III and IV.

guideSections.what: Five grades of disc degeneration from signal, structure, nucleus–annulus distinction and height.
guideSections.howToPerform: On mid-sagittal T2 images assess each disc and choose the grade.

sources.citation: Pfirrmann CWA, Metzdorf A, Zanetti M, Hodler J, Boos N. Magnetic resonance classification of lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration. Spine. 2001;26(17):1873-1878.
